newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO supported by Asian fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO supported by Asian fundamentals.

text.p: Strong Asian fundamentals are expected to support high sulphur fuel oil prices over the Christmas holiday in spite of weaker crude, traders said on Tuesday.

Although the market was dull on Tuesday with most traders having left early for the holiday, the market expects buying support to maintain levels at around Monday's talking levels of $124 per tonne for the 180-cst.
Swaps were largely unchanged with January quoted at $119.50/$121.00 per tonne, compared to $119.75-$120.50 on Monday.
"In the short term, in the month ahead, the picture is not going to change very much," said a Singapore trader.
Traders said Singapore inventories were at low levels as cargoes have been moved to China for its pre-Lunar New Year purchases or gone into the bunker market.
"Bunker demand has been good ahead of the Christmas holiday and the long vacation coming up in Japan," said a trader.
MidEast supplies were healthy with an early January lifting Kuwaiti 380-cst 80,000 tonne cargo sold at above $1.25 per tonne over Singapore quotes on a cost-and-freight basis.

Two traders were also moving their usual VLCC cargoes from the Mideast to Singapore for arrival in January but the flow of oil eastwards is being hampered by the tight freight market in the Mideast, traders said.
